note: Every threshold the app uses. status = validated (checked against an independent source) or assumed (our choice, shown as such in the app).

rules.label: Sun up
rules.description: The Sun counts as up as soon as its upper edge is above the terrain (no atmosphere, so no refraction).
rules.source: LunarNav choice; same convention as sunrise/sunset times

rules.label: Earth in view
rules.description: The Earth counts as in view when any part of its disk is above the terrain.
rules.source: LunarNav choice (direct-to-Earth radio link needs line of sight)

rules.label: Tolerated dark gap
rules.description: Continuous windows bridge dark gaps of this length or less (a battery covers them).
rules.source: LunarNav choice, to be replaced by the battery simulation

rules.label: VIPER rule
rules.description: Longest period with Sun down and Earth down that a solar rover survives.
rules.source: NASA VIPER mission planning (rover survival without Sun and Earth contact)

rules.label: Horizon error margin
rules.description: The whole skyline is raised and lowered by this amount; a verdict that flips is marked close call.
rules.source: LunarNav choice (80 m terrain pixel, observer height)

rules.label: Default mission (battery)
rules.description: Default lander used by the battery simulation; every value can be changed in the Mission panel.
rules.source: LunarNav team, to be checked by Maggie and Edi

rules.label: GO / RISKY / NO-GO

value.noGo: not viable, or VIPER rule broken
value.go: viable and not a close call

rules.description: Viable = continuous window (Sun, plus Earth if required) at least as long as the stay.

validated.label: Sun and Earth directions
validated.description: Largest difference between our Sun/Earth azimuth and elevation and JPL Horizons.
